headline: NovaMind v12 Promises to Feed You a Thunderstorm — Neurologists Urge Caution
body:
Ringo Corporation unveiled NovaMind v12 at a packed Circuit District event this morning, billing it as the first consumer BCI to achieve full-spectrum sensory augmentation — synthetic taste, smell, proprioceptive overlay, and haptic environmental simulation delivered alongside the existing visual and auditory feed. The flagship feature, branded Immersive Sensory Threading or IST, uses SNT conduits to write directly to the thalamic relay layer rather than the cortical surface, meaning the brain receives augmented sensation at the same processing depth as real physical input. Demo attendees described tasting a synthetic rainstorm, smelling a pre-collapse pine forest, and feeling wind pressure that had no physical source. Starting price is 14,800 quanta for the standard implant package, with a 2,400 quanta annual SNT calibration subscription.

The medical community's response was immediate and pointed. Dr. Kenji Okafor-Singh of Helix Biosystems' neural division issued a public advisory within three hours of the announcement, warning that thalamic-depth sensory writing has never been tested in longitudinal consumer trials and that the 'sensation authenticity gap' — the cognitive stress caused when synthetic and real sensory inputs conflict — remains poorly understood at SNT depth. 'We are talking about writing experiences the brain cannot distinguish from physical reality,' Okafor-Singh said in a statement. 'The therapeutic applications are extraordinary. The liability surface is also extraordinary.' Ringo's response cited a 14-month closed beta involving 3,200 participants and a 98.4% satisfaction rating, though it declined to release full adverse event data.

On the street, the reaction in The Circuit and the Gray Zone is predictably split along economic lines. For residents who can afford the implant, the promise of experiencing sensory environments that climate collapse and urban density have made inaccessible — forests, open ocean, unpolluted air — carries obvious appeal. For the majority who cannot, the 14,800 quanta barrier and Ringo's subscription lock-in model represent another tier of experience becoming the exclusive property of those with disposable quanta. The Underground Signal is already calling v12 'the luxury of feeling alive, sold back to you at monthly rates.'

Ringo is targeting full commercial availability by Q1 2193. The Federal Remnant's BCI Regulatory Office has opened a preliminary review but has not indicated any intent to delay the launch.
aftermath: By mid-2194, Helix Biosystems had documented 847 confirmed cases of Sensory Conflict Disorder linked to NovaMind v12 IST use, triggering a Federal Remnant mandatory recall of the thalamic calibration firmware — a recall Ringo contested for eleven months.
runner_relevance: The v12 launch generated a dense runner economy almost immediately. Black-market demand for unsubscribed IST firmware — bypassing Ringo's 2,400 quanta annual calibration fee — created high-volume smuggling contracts moving cracked SNT packages through the Underworld. When the 2194 recall hit, runners were hired for both sides: Ringo contracted extraction teams to recover recalled units from black-market distributors, while independent clinics and Bore Rat medics hired couriers to move uncalibrated units out of Federal Remnant jurisdiction before confiscation sweeps. The adverse event data Helix Biosystems sat on before going public became the most valuable data-retrieval contract in the Circuit that year.
